system.name: KubeDirect
system.one_liner: a modified Kubernetes cluster manager that shortens the narrow-waist control path for serverless (FaaS) scaling with direct message passing

components.name: Custom Controllers
components.role: platform-specific controllers that perform offline configuration for the FaaS orchestrator

components.name: Autoscaler
components.role: computes the desired number of instances from runtime metrics and updates the Deployment replicas field

components.name: Load Balancer
components.role: read-only, downstream gateway and monitoring component that routes traffic to ready Pods

components.name: API Server
components.role: entry point of the K8s core that stores/serves API objects

components.name: etcd
components.role: persistent store backing the API Server

components.name: Core Controllers
components.role: the shared narrow-waist controllers (Deployment/ReplicaSet/Scheduler) that scale FaaS instances

components.name: Kubelet (Sandbox Manager)
components.role: on each worker node, filters locally assigned Pods and forwards them to the sandbox runtime

components.name: Pod
components.role: basic unit of scheduling holding the containers of one FaaS instance

components.name: Runtime
components.role: sandbox runtime that executes the Pod's containers

flows.what: Deployment controller selects the ReplicaSet and sets its replicas field
ReplicaSet controller creates new Pods to match the desired scale
Scheduler assigns Pods to nodes by updating nodeName
marks Pods ready and exposes them to the data plane

content.key_idea: Three popular Kubernetes-based FaaS platforms share a common narrow waist of controllers (highlighted in orange) that implements the critical scale-out path from Autoscaler to running Pod, which is the primary source of latency.
content.reading_order: left FaaS Orchestrator column, right K8s Cluster Manager column, then top-to-bottom following the circled steps 1 through 5 down to the Worker Node and back to the Load Balancer

summary: Figure 2 lays out the architecture of a typical Kubernetes-based FaaS platform, split into a FaaS Orchestrator (Custom Controllers, Autoscaler, Load Balancer) and the underlying K8s Cluster Manager (API Server, etcd, Core Controllers, and a Worker Node running Kubelet, Pod and Runtime). The paper highlights in orange the 'narrow waist' of controllers -- Core Controllers and the Kubelet sandbox manager -- shared by Knative, OpenFaaS and Fission, that implements the critical upscaling path: the Autoscaler computes a target replica count (step 1), the Deployment/ReplicaSet controllers act on it (steps 2-3), the Scheduler and Kubelet place and start Pods (step 4), and the Load Balancer is updated once Pods are ready (step 5). The figure motivates KubeDirect's optimization of this common critical path via direct message passing instead of API-server watch/list overhead.
summary_zh: 图2展示了基于Kubernetes的FaaS平台通用架构，橙色标出的核心控制器与Kubelet是所有平台共有的瓶颈腰部，图中①-⑤标注了从计算副本数到Pod就绪并暴露给负载均衡器的完整关键路径。
